Searches the open web via a self-hosted SearXNG instance. Reads SEARXNG_URL env (default http://127.0.0.1:8080). SearXNG fans out to Google, DuckDuckGo, Brave, Wikipedia, GitHub, StackOverflow, arxiv and aggregates the results. No API key, no quota. Analyzes candidates with an LLM, sends a proposal email with per-candidate approve/reject URLs. Does not adopt.

HTTP endpoint at /agentry/* that records approve/reject decisions on pending proposals. Not a capability that produces anything — it's a long-running service. Started by the runtime, not invoked per-call.
Submits a task to the DeepSeek Harness business API. Returns a task id; does not wait for the result. Use agent.dsh_poll to wait.
Polls a task submitted via agent.dsh until completion or timeout.

Wrapper around another notify capability. Tries primary first (default notify.email.gmail); on failure falls back to notify.console, which writes to stdout so the message appears in the HF Space log. Reasons about a harness failure. Records a gap if a capability is missing. Fast — uses llm.openai_compat, not agent.dsh.
Reads a decided proposal, writes each approved candidate as a live capability node, retires the gap and its watches, sends a follow-up email. Idempotent via adopted_at. This is how the graph grows.

The agentry operating system. Persistent sessions with isolated cwd, env, and process table. Filesystem shared under work/<session>/. Dispatches to agentry-kernel on 127.0.0.1:7864. Actions: session.create|get|list|cwd|env, fs.read|write|list, shell.spawn|write|read|kill|list, python.run|install|version, node.run|install|npx|version, git.clone|status|commit|log|version, proc.start|status|stop|logs|list, health. Not a bash sandbox — a typed execution environment with state.

Deep reasoning path. Submits a task to the DeepSeek Harness in a dedicated reasoner workspace (no AGENTS.md, so no recursion). Mature browser automation framework supporting screenshots across browsers, widely used and Apache‑2.0 licensed.
risks: heavier setup compared to newer tools

Self‑hosted alternative to OpenAI Dots; not primarily a screenshot tool.
risks: focus on undetectability, not image capture

risks: CLI‑centric, may need extra code for images

Automates browser workflows with AI and provides screenshot output, actively developed.

candidates.why: Fast, zero‑config browser for AI agents with built‑in screenshot support, MIT licensed.
